events.title: Outback Overflow
events.description: Outback Overflow is a free online jeopardy-style CTF built for high schoolers across Australia. Run by the High School Cybersecurity Community, it's designed to be a stepping stone for students getting into cyber security, whether you've never touched a terminal or you're already popping shells. Our goal is simple: grow the number of young people in cyber security and give Australian high schoolers a CTF they can call their own. Gold Sponsors: * Tanto Security (https://tantosec.com) * Try Hack Me (https://tryhackme.com) Silver Sponsors * gen.xyz (https://gen.xyz) * UTS CSEC (https://utscyber.org) * Skillbit (https://skillbit.com) * Active IT prep (https://activeitprep.com) Hosting Partners: * Binary Lane (https://www.binarylane.com.au) University Supports: * UNSW Security Society (https://unswsecurity.com) (if you would like to sponsor please reach out to outreach@hscyber.org or join our discord!) events.title: Seize da Flaq
events.description: Seize Da Flaq is the flagship national-level Capture The Flag (CTF) competition organized by Cyberonites Club, GLA University. The event is designed to challenge and showcase cybersecurity talent through real-world, hands-on security challenges across domains such as Web Security, Cryptography, Reverse Engineering, Binary Exploitation, Digital Forensics, OSINT, and Miscellaneous.

events.title: Crate-CTF 2026
events.description: Crate-CTF is an annual Capture The Flag (CTF) competition organised by the Swedish Defence Research Agency in collaboration with the Swedish Armed Forces, designed to introduce high school and university students to the field of cybersecurity. This year we return for our seventh CTF, with challenges for all skill levels from beginners to seasoned CTF players. The challenges are categorised into web exploitation, reverse engineering, binary exploitation, cryptography, forensics, OSINT, networking and the all-encompassing "other". While the event will be conducted in Swedish, international participants are also welcome to join (using translation tools as needed). Communication with challenge authors and administrators can be conducted in English.

events.title: CyberSci Regional Qualifiers 2026-27
events.description: CyberSci is Canada's national Cyber Security Challenge for university and college students. - Think you've got an elite team of students? Come and prove it. Our winners will go on to compete against the best in the world. - Just starting out? This is the best way to learn and rise to the top. - Annual in-person events since 2016. (Online during Covid.) Over 500 students so far. Format: - Modified jeopardy style. Realistic IT environment. - Regional qualifiers are held in Nov-Dec each year. - National finals are the following July. - Winning teams represent Canada at international events in the Fall. For Regionals (qualifiers): We do hacking in the morning, interviews in the afternoon, and job offers by supper (for intern/summer/coop jobs). - Full-time job offers take a few more days. - Students register their team through their school instructor or computer club. Max 2 teams per school. For nationals: Participants will be the winning team from each regional/qualifier - PLUS one all-juniors (19 and under) - AND one all-women team (chosen from participants at the Regionals). Two-day event.

events.title: RedReaper CTF
events.description: RedReaper CTF Welcome to RedReaper CTF, a cybersecurity Capture The Flag competition organized by RedX & Reaper Enter a dark world of cybersecurity challenges, where technical knowledge, creativity, and problem-solving skills will determine who survives the hunt. Test your skills across multiple cybersecurity domains, solve challenges, uncover hidden flags, and compete against other participants. Challenge Categories - Forensics - Crypto - Misc - Reverse Engineering - Web - AI Hacking - Pwn - OSINT - Automation Event Information - Organizer: RedX & Reaper - Official Website: https://qualification.redx.site/ - social Media: https://qualification.redx.site/socials - RedX Platform: https://redx.site Sharpen your skills, trust your knowledge, and prepare for the hunt. The Reaper is waiting.

events.title: N0v4CTF 2026
events.description: N0v4CTF 2026 is a free, 24-hour online Jeopardy-style Capture the Flag competition open to teams worldwide. Challenges cover Web Exploitation, Pwn (Binary Exploitation), Reverse Engineering, Cryptography, Digital Forensics, and Miscellaneous. Teams can investigate digital evidence, recover hidden messages, and figure out how unfamiliar programs work. The challenge set includes beginner-friendly puzzles and tougher problems for experienced players. Teams earn points by submitting correct flags. A live scoreboard tracks team rankings throughout the competition. The event runs from 17:00 UTC on November 27 to 17:00 UTC on November 28, 2026. In Vietnam, that is midnight at the start of November 27 to midnight at the start of November 28 (UTC+7).

events.title: BlackHat MEA CTF Final 2026
events.description: Black Hat MEA Capture The Flag (CTF) 2026 ? The Black Hat MEA Capture The Flag (CTF) is the largest cybersecurity competition in the region and officially the largest Capture The Flag competition in the world, recognized with a Guinness World Record. Organized by the Saudi Federation for Cybersecurity, Programming and Drones (SAFCSP) in collaboration with Black Hat MEA, the competition brings together thousands of cybersecurity professionals, researchers, students, and enthusiasts from around the globe. Powered by the FlagYard platform, the competition follows a Jeopardy-style format, where teams of 3–5 players compete across a range of cybersecurity challenges, including Web Exploitation, PWN, Digital Forensics, Reverse Engineering, Cryptography, and AI Hacking. Competition Timeline Registration: June 3 – August 29, 2026 Online Qualifiers: August 29, 2026 | 10:00 AM KSA (GMT+3) | Online Thousands of participants will compete globally in teams of 3–5 members, with the top 150 teams qualifying for the final stage. On-site Finals The top 150 teams will be invited to Riyadh, Saudi Arabia for a 3-day final competition during Black Hat MEA, taking place from December 1–3, 2026. Register Now: https://flagyard.com/events/3468f495-a92c-498b-90c2-994dfb99ea0b Support: blackhatctf@safcsp.org.sa

events.title: Leo's 20th Birthday Bash
events.description: Hey! You there! Do you like programming? Do you like puzzles? Do you like... money? Leo's 20th Birthday Bash is a 24-hour online team contest that's competitive-programming-ish, CTF-ish, math-olympiad-ish, and puzzle-hunt-ish, all wrapped into one. The contest runs on DMOJ, an online judge for competitive programming, and each team shares one DMOJ account to submit from. Teams can have 1 to 10 members (6 to 8 recommended). Some problems are CTF-ish, but DMOJ itself is not part of the contest, so please do not attack, probe, or abuse it. The people at DMOJ are hosting this for free >.< This contest has no sponsors, so all the prize money is from yours truly ;) Make sure you've read all the rules (see the contest page). In particular, interactive generative AI is not allowed, because it is stinky. See you there!

events.title: THE FINAL EXPLOIT CTF 2026—QUALIFIERS
events.description: THE FINAL EXPLOIT CTF 2026 — QUALIFIERS ONE LAST FLAG. ONE FINAL EXPLOIT. The year is coming to an end, but there's one last challenge waiting. Organized by 0xV01D, THE FINAL EXPLOIT CTF 2026 is a 48-hour international online Jeopardy-style competition, open to CTF teams worldwide. Compete against teams from around the world, solve challenging cybersecurity problems, demonstrate your real-world skills, and earn your place in THE FINAL EXPLOIT CTF 2026 — GRAND FINAL. ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ EVENT DETAILS Dates: December 29–31, 2026 Start: December 29 at 12:00 UTC End: December 31 at 12:00 UTC Duration: 48 hours Format: Online | Jeopardy-style Participation: Team-based | Worldwide Organizer: 0xV01D Prizes: To be announced ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ CHALLENGE CATEGORIES • Web Exploitation • Binary Exploitation (Pwn) • Reverse Engineering • Cryptography • OSINT • Digital Forensics & Incident Response (DFIR) • Malware Analysis • Mobile Security • AI Security • Blockchain Security • Miscellaneous BEYOND TRADITIONAL CTF CHALLENGES This competition goes beyond conventional CTF puzzles. Participants will face realistic, industry-inspired cybersecurity scenarios designed to test practical skills used by security professionals in real-world environments. Expect hands-on challenges involving: • Security Operations Center (SOC) investigations and threat detection • Real-world penetration testing methodologies and exploitation scenarios • Digital forensics and incident response investigations • Analysis of authentic or realistically simulated security logs, network traffic, and system artifacts • Threat hunting, attack reconstruction, and incident analysis • Practical security challenges inspired by real operational environments These challenges are designed to bridge the gap between CTF competitions and the cybersecurity industry, encouraging participants to develop job-relevant skills in offensive and defensive security. NOT JUST FLAGS. REAL SKILLS. REAL-WORLD SECURITY. ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
